entities.name: Abdul Rahman Arif
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abdul Rahman Mohammed ʿArif al-Jumayli, better known as Abdul Rahman Arif, was an Iraqi military officer and politician who served as the third president of Iraq from 16 April 1966 to 17 July 1968. Born on April 14, 1916, in Baghdad, he emerged as a significant figure during the turbulent Modern era of industrialization, imperial expansion, and democratic revolutions that reshaped the Middle East.

Arif was the older brother of Abdul Salam Arif, the second president of Iraq, whom he succeeded after his brother died in an airplane crash in 1966. This succession exemplified the dynastic traditions and sovereign authority mechanisms that characterized mid-twentieth century Iraq. Following the 1968 Bath Party coup, Abdul Rahman Arif was deposed and spent his final years in exile before his death in 2007. His presidency represented a critical period in Iraq's post-independence history, marked by the country's struggle to establish stable governance amid Cold War tensions and regional geopolitical conflicts.

As a key figure in the political systems and empire and colonialism frameworks of the Modern era, Arif's legacy reflects the complex interplay between military authority and civilian governance. His rule contributed to the establishment of dynastic legacies and territorial boundaries that would influence Iraqi and broader Middle Eastern politics for decades to come. Through his involvement in the Monarchs & Rulers category of historical figures, Abdul Rahman Arif remains an important subject of study for understanding the foundations of the contemporary global order.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the third president of Iraq from 1966 to 1968, Abdul Rahman Arif played a pivotal role in shaping the country's politics during a period of significant turmoil and transformation. His presidency was marked by a brief but decisive impact on Iraq's future trajectory.
